quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for cars with a certain number of people inside.
Only certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for cars with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is reserved for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisle next to a handicap parking space?
questions.explanation: You cannot park in the access aisle next to a handicap space. This space is needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Only cars with special disability plates or placards can park in handicap parking spaces marked with an official sign.
questions.explanation: Only vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards can use reserved disability parking spaces.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the road at night, use your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when the way is clear.

questions.question: If your car has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: Sit at least 10 inches away from the steering wheel.
Tilt the steering wheel down so it points at your chest, not your head.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seatbelt. Sit at least 10 inches from the steering wheel. Tilt the wheel downward if you can so it aims at your chest instead of your head or neck.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly that they seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive poorly in ways that look like drunk driving. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert and safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must stop completely and wait for all traffic and pedestrians to clear before driving forward.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is coming, move to the right side of the road as far as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies no matter which direction the emergency vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is jaywalking.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is jaywalking.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: In Virginia, what are the curfew hours when drivers under 18 cannot drive?
questions.explanation: If you are under 18, you cannot drive between midnight and 4 a.m., with some exceptions.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol in a person's body.

questions.question: Radar detectors are illegal in Virginia.
questions.explanation: Virginia law makes it illegal to use a radar detector.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop at an intersection. You must yield to other drivers and pedestrians. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you and them.
Brake hard to force them to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors constantly to notice tailgaters. If a car is following too closely, slow down gradually or change lanes to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means you cannot do the action shown. In this case, no right turns are allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must or must not do. It means parking is not permitted in this area.

questions.question: What increases a driver's risk of crashing?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players all distract drivers and increase the risk of crashing.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You can only cross them when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: What should you do at a yield sign?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Yield only to traffic on your right.
Yield only to traffic on your left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection go before you enter.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed the whole time.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay close to the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve, then gradually speed up as you leave it. Speeding up while entering a curve makes it harder to control your car.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that side. A solid yellow line means passing is not allowed from that side.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: What is hardest to see at night?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are much harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic goes in both directions. You may pass, but only if it is safe and you will not hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: No one may pass from either direction.
Everyone may pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one may pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooters, or skateboards when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells you an island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: If you are not in the correct lane for your turn at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes, then put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side with a median.
